title: Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship (SURF), Engineering
summary: 8-week summer lab research for about 15 fellows, plus graduate-school preparation, for students interested in an engineering PhD. GPA 3.0 or higher. First-generation and low-income students are especially encouraged.
citizenship: Open to US students; international students enrolled full-time at a US college (with CPT/OPT) are eligible
international_note: Only if enrolled full-time at a US college; students living outside the US are not eligible.

title: Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowships (SURF)
summary: 10 weeks of in-person summer research with a Caltech faculty mentor. Students write a research proposal with their mentor. Check the eligibility page for who can apply from other schools.

title: MIT Summer Research Program (MSRP)
summary: Summer research with MIT faculty (June 7 to August 7, 2027), with weekly seminars, a research paper, a poster and help writing a graduate-school statement. Aims to broaden participation in research. Applications due January 19.

title: Chemers Neustein Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship (SURF)
summary: 10 weeks of lab research (June 7 to August 13, 2027) in biochemistry, structural and cell biology, immunology, virology, neuroscience, physics or mathematical biology. About 25 students are chosen from 700+ applicants.

title: Summer Research Opportunities Program (SROP)
summary: Faculty-mentored summer research at Big Ten universities with weekly enrichment sessions, ending in a symposium. Each campus runs its own program; check the campus pages for pay, eligibility and dates.

title: Summer Research Early Identification Program (SR-EIP)
summary: Summer research at partner universities from a national consortium that works to build a research workforce reflecting the diversity of the country. Check the program page for pay, eligibility and dates.

title: Summer Undergraduate Research in Engineering (SURE)
summary: 10-week summer research (May 23 to July 30, 2027) for students thinking about graduate school in engineering or science. All students may apply. Decisions by April 1, 2027.

title: Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship (SURF), Engineering
summary: Paid 10-week research program with research symposia. Open to Purdue students, students at other US colleges and students at international universities. International applicants are due December 15, 2026; everyone else has a January 15, 2027 priority deadline, then rolling.
pay: $6,500 + $2,500 housing allowance and travel help for non-Purdue students
citizenship: Open to US and international students

title: International Student Research Internship Program
org: Washington University in St. Louis, McKelvey School of Engineering
summary: 10 weeks of summer engineering research for students at universities outside the US, in their second-to-last undergraduate year. The last posted cycle (summer 2026) closed November 13, 2025; check the page for the next cycle.
pay: $3,000 + free housing and transit pass (student pays airfare, visa, insurance, food)
citizenship: Only for non-US citizens / non-permanent residents
international_note: For students enrolled at universities outside the US.

title: HBCU-Berkeley Environmental Scholars for Change
org: UC Berkeley, Environmental Science, Policy and Management
summary: Two months of justice-centered environmental research (June 1 to July 31, 2027) with Berkeley mentors in agri-food systems, biodiversity, climate, water or health. Designed for HBCU students.
citizenship: Open to HBCU students, including DACA and international students

title: Du Bois Scholars Program
summary: Fully funded 9-week summer research with Harvard faculty, matched to the student's field, for students from selected R1, R2 and research-focused HBCUs. Includes a stipend and housing.

title: UC-HBCU Neuroscience Pathways Program
summary: 8-week summer placement in UCLA labs (June 14 to August 6, 2027) with a poster competition, for students at HBCUs, with a focus on neuroscience and physiology.

title: Davidson Research Initiative for HBCU Students
summary: A mentored summer research project with a Davidson faculty member for rising juniors and seniors from HBCUs. The last posted deadline was March 16, 2026; check the page for the 2027 cycle.
pay: $600 a week + up to $1,000 for supplies or travel

title: BRIDGE UP Summer Research Program
org: University of Utah, Center for Clinical and Translational Science
summary: 10 weeks of summer translational research with clinical shadowing, for students from colleges with limited research opportunities.
